title: A middle people
hookLine: We made you a community of the middle way (2:143)
last: WHAT WILL YOU KEEP AFTER ME.

lines: TWO HUNDRED EIGHTY-SIX, DIVIDED BY TWO.
THE MIDDLE VERSE, ABOUT THE MIDDLE.
cards: Al-Baqarah has two hundred eighty-six verses. Divide by two, and you land on verse one hundred forty-three.

Many readers have noticed that the verse in the middle of the longest surah is the verse about being in the middle. Whether that's design or coincidence, the Qur'an doesn't say, and scholars don't build anything on it.
But it makes the verse easy to find, and it fits what the verse says. Today: wasat.

teach.b: Last year you met this verse in the story of the qiblah turning toward Mecca. This year, look at one word. In Pickthall's words: “Thus We have appointed you a middle nation.”

teach.h: THE MIDDLE IS THE BEST PART
teach.b: Wasat means the middle, the center, but in Arabic the middle is also the best part: the middle of the valley, where the water runs; the middle of the family, the most honored.

A hadith in Bukhari explains the word in this very verse with one other: 'adl, just, balanced. The verse gives a reason: a middle people, so that you may be witnesses over humanity, and the messenger a witness over you.

teach.h: A WITNESS STANDS WHERE BOTH SIDES SHOW
teach.b: A witness has to stand where both sides can be seen; you can't see the whole field from one end zone. So what does the middle look like in a life?
Bukhari tells of three men who asked about the Prophet's worship and found it less than they expected. One said: I'll pray all night, every night. Another: I'll fast every day.

teach.h: I FAST AND I EAT, I PRAY AND I SLEEP
teach.b: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ came to them and said, in effect: I'm the most mindful of God among you, and I fast and I eat, I pray and I sleep, and I marry. Whoever turns from my way is not of me. The middle isn't lukewarm.
It's the balance that lets someone keep going for a lifetime, and see both sides clearly enough to be a fair witness.

how: Muslim scholars often cite 2:143 and the hadith of the three men in Bukhari when teaching moderation in worship: steady, sustainable practice rather than extremes of devotion or neglect.

o: a halfway rest stop on the pilgrim road to Mecca
lukewarm: never too committed to anything at all
the middle, which in Arabic is also the best and most just

p: the middle, the best, the just
how a hadith in Bukhari explains wasat
stands where both sides can be seen
all night, every day, never marry

s: in Arabic the middle is also the best part, and a hadith explains it as just.
verse 143 sits at the midpoint of al-Baqarah's 286 verses
readers have noticed it; scholars don't build a teaching on it.

games.q: three men vow: pray all night, fast every day, never marry. the Prophet hears. what does he say?
o: well done, all three of you.
I fast and I eat, I pray and I sleep, and I marry.
only the first vow is allowed.
games.why: he points to his own balanced way, and says whoever turns from it is not of him. the middle is the way that lasts.

practice: Look for one place in your life that has drifted to an end: working every evening, scrolling past midnight, swearing off sugar forever, or doing nothing at all for something you care about.
Picture its middle, not zero and not everything, the amount you could keep up for a year, and rest there for a few breaths.

wordCard.voice: Wasat. The middle: in Arabic, also the best and the most just. Al-Baqarah calls the Muslim community a middle nation, so it can be a fair witness. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the middle, the center; also the best and most balanced. ummatan wasatan in 2:143.
